The name of a class declaration can be assigned to like a `let` variable. After that the class is gone, and every `new Logger()` and `instanceof Logger` in the file works with the new value. That is almost always a mistake.

This rule is on by default in JavaScript files. It is off in TypeScript files, where TypeScript reports the same mistake.

## Examples

Reported:

{/* bad */}
```js
class Logger {}

Logger = createLogger();
```

Not reported:

{/* good */}
```js
class Logger {}

const logger = createLogger();
```

A variable that holds a class expression is an ordinary variable:

{/* good */}
```js
let Store = class {};

Store = class extends Store {};
```
